title: Complete norm coefficients preserve torsion-acyclic principal-open restriction
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and let $B$ be a complete nonarchimedean normed field extending $\mathbf Q_\ell$ isometrically [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]; completeness means completeness for $d(x,y)=|x-y|$. Put $O=\{b\in B:|b|\leq1\}$ and $O_n=O/\ell^nO$ for $n\geq1$, with each $O_n$ discrete. Let $V$ be an affine scheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum] whose terminal object on its small pro-etale site is weakly contractible [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, sk-def-pe-weak-contractible], let $f\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, and put $T=V[1/f]$. Assume that for every $n\geq1$ and abelian group $M$ killed by $\ell^n$, the actual restriction $R\Gamma(V,\underline M_V[0])\to R\Gamma(T,\underline M_T[0])$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$, where $\underline M_Z$ is the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf].

For $Z=V,T$ write $C_{B,Z}=p_Z^*C_B$, with $C_B(P)=C(P,B)$ for every profinite set $P$, using all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $L_Z=p_Z^*C_O$, with $C_O(P)=C(P,O)$ for the subspace topology of $O\subset B$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]; since $p_Z^*$ is exact and $C_O\to C_B$ (postcomposition with the inclusion) is a monomorphism, $L_Z$ is a subsheaf of $C_{B,Z}$ (the subsheaf of $O$-valued functions). There are canonical sheaf identifications
$$L_Z\cong\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\underline{O_n}_Z,\qquad C_{B,Z}\cong\varinjlim_{m\geq0}(L_Z\xrightarrow{\ell}L_Z\xrightarrow{\ell}\cdots),$$
with quotient projections in the first and stage-$m$ insertion $x\mapsto\ell^{-m}x$ in the second [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit, def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The transition maps $\underline{O_{n+1}}_Z\to\underline{O_n}_Z$ are epimorphisms, and the canonical map
$$L_Z[0]\longrightarrow R\varprojlim_n\underline{O_n}_Z[0]$$
is an isomorphism in the ordinary derived category of abelian sheaves [def-weil-derived-limit, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived sections mean K-injective derived sections of underlying abelian sheaves [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. The actual restriction maps for both $L$ and $C_B$ are isomorphisms in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$; in particular
$$R\Gamma(V,C_{B,V}[0])\longrightarrow R\Gamma(T,C_{B,T}[0])$$
is an isomorphism and $H^q(T,C_{B,T})=0$ for $q>0$. All identifications commute with restriction and the displayed quotient and multiplication maps. No local compactness of $B$, finiteness of $O_n$, or finite-subfield descent is assumed. Empty $V,T$ and the identity open are included.

Agent-formulated sublemma; the complete retained argument and its existing citations are in report.md, not a theorem attributed to the blueprint.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-totally-disconnected-coefficient-realization] for $B$, its unit ball $O$, and the discrete rings $O_n$: nonarchimedean balls are clopen, so these spaces are Hausdorff and totally disconnected. Naturality and compatibility with finite products identify the additive and multiplicative operations as well as all quotient and inclusion maps. Thus on every pro-etale object $U$ the three coefficient sheaves have sections $C(|U|,B)$, $C(|U|,O)$ and $C(|U|,O_n)$; the last is the constant sheaf. The pointwise inclusion makes $L_Z$ a subsheaf of $C_{B,Z}$. This also verifies that their restrictions to the open $T$ use the prescribed coefficient maps.

source.place: Paragraph (3), complete norm-coefficient test: unit-ball quotients, epimorphic derived inverse limit, and multiplication-by-ell rationalization. Agent elaboration of Bhatt--Scholze Lemmas 4.2.12 and 6.8.2; not a theorem stated by the blueprint.

proof.text: The additive metric group $O$ is complete because it is closed in $B$. Put $U_n=\ell^nO$. Multiplicativity of the norm and $|\ell|=\ell^{-1}$ give $U_n=\{x\in B:|x|\leq\ell^{-n}\}$. These are open additive subgroups: a sufficiently small open ball about each member stays in $U_n$ by the ultrametric inequality. They decrease and their diameters tend to zero. Apply [lem-sfb-complete-metric-group-quotients] to this group and these subgroups. It identifies $C(|U|,O)$ with the compatible families of $C(|U|,O_n)$ for every object $U$, by exactly the quotient projections. Together with step 1 this is the asserted sheaf isomorphism $L_Z\cong\varprojlim_n\underline{O_n}_Z$, natural in restriction.

source.place: Paragraph (3), complete norm-coefficient test: unit-ball quotients, epimorphic derived inverse limit, and multiplication-by-ell rationalization. Agent elaboration of Bhatt--Scholze Lemmas 4.2.12 and 6.8.2; not a theorem stated by the blueprint.

proof.text: Each map $\underline{O_{n+1}}_Z\to\underline{O_n}_Z$ is an epimorphism. Indeed a section is a continuous $O_n$-valued function by step 1; its inverse images of points form an open cover, and on each piece the function is constant and lifts to any representative in $O_{n+1}$. This proves local surjectivity, hence epimorphy by [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective]. Apply [det-pe-continuous-cohomology-limit] on each of the schemes $Z=V,T$ to obtain both the canonical isomorphism $L_Z[0]\to R\varprojlim_n\underline{O_n}_Z[0]$ and $R\Gamma(Z,L_Z[0])\cong R\varprojlim_nR\Gamma(Z,\underline{O_n}_Z[0])$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), complete norm-coefficient test: unit-ball quotients, epimorphic derived inverse limit, and multiplication-by-ell rationalization. Agent elaboration of Bhatt--Scholze Lemmas 4.2.12 and 6.8.2; not a theorem stated by the blueprint.

proof.text: Every additive group $O_n$ is killed by $\ell^n$, regardless of its cardinality. The hypothesis therefore makes the restriction map on each $R\Gamma(-,\underline{O_n}[0])$ an isomorphism. These maps commute with transitions because they are actual restrictions. Applying the derived inverse-limit functor to this isomorphism of towers and using step 3 proves that the actual restriction $R\Gamma(V,L_V[0])\to R\Gamma(T,L_T[0])$ is an isomorphism. Naturality of the canonical comparison in [det-pe-continuous-cohomology-limit] identifies the resulting map with restriction, rather than an unspecified isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph (3), complete norm-coefficient test: unit-ball quotients, epimorphic derived inverse limit, and multiplication-by-ell rationalization. Agent elaboration of Bhatt--Scholze Lemmas 4.2.12 and 6.8.2; not a theorem stated by the blueprint.

proof.text: For an affine object $U$ of $Z_{\mathrm{proet}}$, any continuous $b:|U|\to B$ has bounded norm. Indeed the increasing open sets $\{x:|b(x)|<\ell^m\}$ cover $|U|$, and quasi-compactness gives one bound. Consequently $\ell^m b$ takes values in $O$ for some $m\geq0$. The inclusions $x\mapsto\ell^{-m}x$ are injective and satisfy $\ell^{-(m+1)}(\ell x)=\ell^{-m}x$. Hence their union on $U$ is all $C(|U|,B)$. For the small filtered index $\mathbf N$, [det-pe-bounded-continuity-sections] in degree zero, applied to the complexes $L_Z[0]$, says evaluation of their sheaf colimit on this affine $U$ is that union. The canonical colimit map to $C_{B,Z}$ is therefore bijective on affine objects; cover any object by affines and glue to conclude it is a sheaf isomorphism. This proves the prescribed rationalization formula with its actual stage insertions.

source.place: Paragraph (3), complete norm-coefficient test: unit-ball quotients, epimorphic derived inverse limit, and multiplication-by-ell rationalization. Agent elaboration of Bhatt--Scholze Lemmas 4.2.12 and 6.8.2; not a theorem stated by the blueprint.

proof.text: Both $V$ and its principal open $T$ are affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply [det-pe-bounded-continuity-sections] in every degree to the multiplication-by-$\ell$ sequence $L_Z[0]$, uniformly concentrated in degrees at least zero. By step 5 it gives $H^q(Z,C_{B,Z})\cong\varinjlim_m H^q(Z,L_Z)$ for every integer $q$. The identifications commute with the restriction from $V$ to $T$ and with the multiplication maps, since they are induced by the colimit cocones. Step 4 makes every stage restriction an isomorphism; their colimit is thus an isomorphism in each degree. This proves that the actual derived restriction for $C_B$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), complete norm-coefficient test: unit-ball quotients, epimorphic derived inverse limit, and multiplication-by-ell rationalization. Agent elaboration of Bhatt--Scholze Lemmas 4.2.12 and 6.8.2; not a theorem stated by the blueprint.

proof.text: The weak contractibility assumed for the terminal object of $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ makes evaluation at $V$ exact: limits of sheaves are computed sectionwise, and an epimorphism of abelian sheaves is locally surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective], hence is an epimorphism on underlying set sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective]; [sk-def-pe-weak-contractible] then gives surjectivity on sections. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], evaluation on $C_{B,V}[0]$ computes its K-injective derived sections and is concentrated in degree zero. Step 6 therefore gives $H^q(T,C_{B,T})=0$ for $q>0$. All constructions used quotient maps, precomposition and the displayed stage insertions, proving the requested compatibility. Empty schemes have zero abelian sections; for the identity open all restriction maps used above are identities. Neither argument excludes these cases.
